rule: good. the rule line is never parsed and needs no rewrite; only the first sentence needs a change.
texts: bad: 'the cove water' is a bare noun-noun compound, so the translator invented a containment link — the water being located inside the cove — that your words never state, whereas the sibling sentence's 'the cove's water' gets the correct part-of-the-cove link. Rewrite as: "When a lantern at the Sunken Cove dies before dawn, a wraith emerges from the cove's water."

good. explicit 'whenever', one finite clause per side, and the possessive 'the cove's water' — this gives a fireable rule with every participant covered, and is the shape to copy for the rest of the item.
good. the modified bare plural becomes a fireable blanket denial over lanterns away from the cove, with the restriction carried as a condition and nothing added or lost.

good. the name, the cove kind, 'drowned' and the village link all land and nothing is invented; only the identifying force of 'the village's ... graveyard' (that this is the village's one graveyard) has no encoding, and no rewording of the sentence would carry it.
